description:
src/crl.rs:101-104, src/ocsp.rs:104-110, src/cache.rs:640-643/809-815, async_crl.rs:79-81, async_ocsp.rs:79-85: every all-URLs-failed path constructs `RevocationFetchFailed { description: format!("all {} URL(s) failed: {}", N, joined) }`. The per-URL details — URL, FetchError variant, status code — are baked into a String.

Operator scenarios that the unstructured format defeats:
- 'Alert me if any single OCSP URL hits >50% 503 rate' — must regex-scrape the description string.
- 'Retry the URL that failed with HTTP 502, skip the one that failed with TLS error' — same.
- 'Track per-CA OCSP availability' — same.

Maintenance consequence: every consumer that wants telemetry will either parse the description string (fragile to format drift), or implement their own RevocationChecker wrapper that bypasses the all-failed aggregation. The crate could expose a structured form:

    pub struct PerUrlFailure { pub url: String, pub error: FetchOrParseError }

and wrap it as either a new Error variant or as RevocationFetchFailed { failures: Vec<PerUrlFailure> } — the latter is a pkix-revocation::Error change, out of scope. The former — adding a new variant — could be done downstream of #non_exhaustive being already on pkix_revocation::Error.

Recommendation: leave description as a fallback string, but propose a follow-up in pkix-revocation to add a RevocationFetchFailedWithFailures { failures: Vec<...> } variant and have the http crate emit the new variant. Cross-crate change. Track separately.
title: RevocationFetchFailed.description is unstructured — operators can't telemetry per-URL failures
